brief.greeting: Good morning. ESP32 now has a traffic light for staying online, and nobody needed a traffic cop.

stories.headline: Baidu drops ERNIE‑5.5‑Flash preview
stories.body: **New text generator lands:** Baidu posted ERNIE‑5.5‑Flash‑Preview on Hugging Face, already pulled 2,609 downloads and 394 likes. It’s a flash‑fast, 2‑stage transformer for quick prompts.
stories.why: If you prototype LLM pipelines, this model gives you a ready‑made, lightweight baseline.

stories.headline: Kandinsky‑ImageSR‑2.0 ups image quality
stories.body: **Upscaling gets a boost:** Kandinskylab released ImageSR‑2.0 on Hugging Face, an image‑to‑image upscaler that has been downloaded 582 times and earned 213 likes. It sharpens details without hallucinating new content.
stories.why: For vision research, it offers a plug‑and‑play super‑resolution head you can benchmark instantly.

stories.headline: Friday patches hit major Linux distros
stories.body: **Critical fixes roll out:** LWN reports Friday security updates across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora and others, covering kernels, MariaDB, nginx and other core packages. The patches close known remote‑code‑execution vectors.
stories.why: Keeping your dev boxes patched avoids surprise break‑ins during on‑call rotations.

highlights.title: ESP32 Remote Access Done Light
highlights.summary: Pinscope’s team built ESP32 Remote Access Done Light to keep an ESP32 securely connected to a server despite limited RAM.
highlights.detail: The project solves a common embedded‑system issue by offloading heavy networking tasks, enabling reliable remote access for low‑resource devices. Source code and schematics are shared on Hackaday.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Friday security updates were issued for many Linux distributions, covering kernels, MariaDB, nginx, and other critical packages across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, and more.
highlights.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities in core system components and popular services, requiring administrators to apply patches promptly. Each distro’s advisory lists specific CVE identifiers and version bumps.

highlights.title: A Detailed Breakdown of the 2021 Texas Power Crisis
highlights.summary: Hackaday published a detailed breakdown of the February 2021 Texas power crisis, examining the grid’s emergency measures and failures.
highlights.detail: The analysis outlines how the grid operator exhausted all available safeguards, the sequence of rolling blackouts, and the long‑term lessons for grid resilience. It includes data visualizations of demand versus supply.

highlights.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 396: Robot Hands, The Inner Life of Mechanical Watches, and the Truth about 3D Scanning
highlights.summary: Hackaday Podcast Episode 396 covers robot hands, mechanical watch internals, and 3D scanning misconceptions.
highlights.detail: The episode features editors Elliot and Al Williams discussing recent hardware projects, including a new robotic hand prototype, a deep dive into the mechanics of vintage watches, and a critical look at common 3D scanning myths.

related.title: Building a Robotic Hand on a Budget

highlights.title: How to Make a Nixie Tube
highlights.summary: Polymatt built a functional Nixie tube over two weeks, documenting the process.
highlights.detail: The maker recreated the classic neon-filled display by fabricating the glass envelope, assembling the cathode elements, and sealing the tube, providing a step‑by‑step guide for hobbyists interested in retro electronics.
